proposed_statement_changes.reason: Literal convergence of the labelled covariance matrix is not invariant to the eigenvector signs allowed by the frozen merely measurable convention. At sign-chart boundaries the empirical covariance may converge only after signed-row conjugation, while its Gaussian norm quantile and the symmetrized confidence set remain invariant. The proposed claim states exactly this weaker orbit-consistency and preserves all count-coverage and contraction conclusions.

proposed_core_edits.reason: FOBI is computed after centering and whitening, so its eigenvalues depend on centered standardized fourth cumulants. The frozen raw-moment ratio is not shift invariant: shifted identically distributed Laplace errors can satisfy distinct frozen values while their centered FOBI eigenvalues coincide.
The proof uses the published square-ICA uniqueness result and the frozen stable-orbit definition directly; both must appear in the declared proof spine.

proposed.justification: The proposition closes the identification step that turns a matrix-representative count into a causal functional of the observational law.
proposed.gap: The ICA literature states sign, scale, and permutation indeterminacy, but stable-orbit counting requires an explicit normalization-preserving bijection across representatives.
proposed.consumer: Any population or sample procedure may start from an arbitrary ICA labeling without changing the reported stable count.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The narrowed orbit-covariance statement needs the published FOBI pointwise limit in its declared spine; the remaining dependencies support normalization, symmetrization, count inversion, and population representative invariance.

proposed.justification: Region-first inversion respects ICA indeterminacy and avoids differentiating an integer-valued functional.
proposed.gap: Miettinen et al. stop at a labelled FOBI matrix limit, while generic set-inversion work does not handle the monomial ICA orbit and Schur-normalization discontinuities.
proposed.consumer: Applied cyclic-LiNG analyses can report count uncertainty without claiming uniform support recovery or selecting an arbitrary ICA labeling.
